Here's Python code using Altair to create visualizations with the Seattle weather dataset:

## Basic Setup and Data Loading

```python
import altair as alt
import pandas as pd

# Load the dataset
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vega/vega/master/docs/data/seattle-weather.csv"
weather = pd.read_csv(url)

# Parse the date column
weather['date'] = pd.to_datetime(weather['date'])

# Enable Altair to render in Jupyter notebooks
alt.data_transformers.enable('json')
```

## Common Visualizations

### 1. Temperature Over Time
```python
# Line chart of temperature over time
temp_chart = alt.Chart(weather).mark_line().add_params(
).encode(
    x='date:T',
    y='temp_max:Q',
    color=alt.Color('weather:N', legend=alt.Legend(title="Weather Type"))
).properties(
    width=600,
    height=300,
    title="Seattle Temperature Over Time"
)

temp_chart.show()
```

### 2. Precipitation Bar Chart
```python
# Bar chart of precipitation by month
precip_chart = alt.Chart(weather).mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X('month(date):O', title='Month'),
    y=alt.Y('mean(precipitation):Q', title='Average Precipitation'),
    color=alt.Color('mean(precipitation):Q', scale=alt.Scale(scheme='blues'))
).properties(
    width=400,
    height=300,
    title="Average Monthly Precipitation in Seattle"
)

precip_chart.show()
```

### 3. Weather Distribution
```python
# Pie chart of weather conditions
weather_dist = alt.Chart(weather).mark_arc().encode(
    theta=alt.Theta("count()", type="quantitative"),
    color=alt.Color("weather:N", legend=alt.Legend(title="Weather Type")),
).properties(
    width=300,
    height=300,
    title="Distribution of Weather Conditions"
)

weather_dist.show()
```

### 4. Temperature vs Precipitation Scatter Plot
```python
# Scatter plot with interactive selection
brush = alt.selection_interval()

scatter = alt.Chart(weather).mark_circle(size=60).add_params(
    brush
).encode(
    x=alt.X('temp_max:Q', title='Max Temperature (°C)'),
    y=alt.Y('precipitation:Q', title='Precipitation (mm)'),
    color=alt.condition(brush, 'weather:N', alt.value('lightgray')),
    tooltip=['date:T', 'temp_max:Q', 'precipitation:Q', 'weather:N']
).properties(
    width=400,
    height=300,
    title="Temperature vs Precipitation"
)

scatter.show()
```

### 5. Seasonal Heatmap
```python
# Heatmap of temperature by month and year
heatmap = alt.Chart(weather).mark_rect().encode(
    x=alt.X('month(date):O', title='Month'),
    y=alt.Y('year(date):O', title='Year'),
    color=alt.Color('mean(temp_max):Q', 
                   scale=alt.Scale(scheme='warmcool'),
                   title='Avg Max Temp'),
    tooltip=['month(date):O', 'year(date):O', 'mean(temp_max):Q']
).properties(
    width=600,
    height=400,
    title="Temperature Heatmap by Month and Year"
)

heatmap.show()
```

### 6. Multi-Panel Dashboard
```python
# Create a dashboard with multiple charts
base = alt.Chart(weather)

# Temperature line chart
temp_line = base.mark_line().encode(
    x='month(date):O',
    y='mean(temp_max):Q',
    color=alt.value('red')
).properties(width=200, height=150, title="Temperature")

# Precipitation bars
precip_bars = base.mark_bar().encode(
    x='month(date):O',
    y='mean(precipitation):Q',
    color=alt.value('blue')
).properties(width=200, height=150, title="Precipitation")

# Wind speed area chart
wind_area = base.mark_area().encode(
    x='month(date):O',
    y='mean(wind):Q',
    color=alt.value('green')
).properties(width=200, height=150, title="Wind Speed")

# Combine charts
dashboard = alt.hconcat(temp_line, precip_bars, wind_area).resolve_scale(
    y='independent'
).properties(
    title="Seattle Weather Dashboard"
)

dashboard.show()
```

## Dataset Info
The Seattle weather dataset typically contains these columns:
- `date`: Date of observation
- `precipitation`: Precipitation amount
- `temp_max`: Maximum temperature
- `temp_min`: Minimum temperature  
- `wind`: Wind speed
- `weather`: Weather condition (sun, rain, snow, etc.)

Each visualization demonstrates different Altair features like encoding channels, marks, transformations, and interactivity. You can modify the code based on your specific analysis needs!
